messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: 2045678901 — automated alert: p99 latency > SLO (streaming) in eu-west-1. Source: infra.metrics (streaming-tail). Investigating.

ajay: picking this up — I'm oncall. seeing p99 jump to ~2.8s from baseline 420ms. streaming stalls (partial responses) reported.

maria: pls post any logs. are we seeing NVME errors or GPU soft ECC counts increasing?

jordan: quick snapshot: node-gpu-124 in pool-inference-eu shows rising ECC multi-bit counts. nvidia-smi shows ECC errors incrementing, then GPU dropped to 50% clocks. suspect thermal/ECC cascade.

ajay: thanks. running `kubectl drain node-gpu-124 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` now to migrate pods. will set `max-surge` to avoid overload.

lisa: FYI customer-facing streaming endpoints are routed across 3 nodes, one of which is this GPU. We have automatic fallback to smaller model on CPU but streaming codepath doesn't fallback cleanly — that's why stalls show up.

oliver: any impacted customers identified yet? CS dashboard shows elevated error rates for org-amber and org-verdant. Request volume for amber is ~120rps, 14% of their requests hit p99>2s.

ajay: draining done. pods moving — but saw a couple resumable stalls in logs while draining. running `kubectl cordon node-gpu-124` to keep it out of rotation.

jordan: past logs from dmesg: `GPU 0: ECC multi-bit error detected, count=17` then `thermal_throttle: GPU0 downclock to 600MHz` within 30s. attaching snippet:

```
[ 12345.678901] nvidia 0000:65:00.0: GPU ECC multi-bit error detected: 17
[ 12346.012345] kernel: nv_host: gpu0: thermal_event: throttle start
[ 12346.094321] containerd: stream-server[pid=2345]: stall detected: p99_stream_latency=2790ms
```

maria: opsbot, pull latest nvidia-smi output and GPU metrics for node-gpu-124.

opsbot: Pulling metrics... 
metrics dump: nv_smi_ecc_count: 18, temp=92C, pow_draw=280W, clocks=600/2100, driver=525.85.12

ajay: temp 92C — that's high. Is there airflow/thermal sensor anomaly on host? Infra telemetry shows CPU fans at 100% but intake temp still rising. Possible rack cooling failure or clogged filter.

lisa: immediate mitigation: 1) cordon node (done), 2) enable model fallback to smaller-medium variant in eu-west-1 for streaming routes for next 10m, 3) increase prefetch/concurrency limits per-instance to avoid queue pileup. ajay, can you patch routing?

ajay: pushed a temporary route override: `route: streaming-eu-west -> prefer model-x-small` for 10m. Applying QoS: `max_concurrency=8` for streaming workers in eu-west.

oliver: notifying customers: I'll ping org-amber and org-verdant with ETA ~20m. Marking incident as "degraded" not outage.

jordan: curious note — ECC counts jumped before thermal spike, could be flaky DIMM or GPU memory module starting to fail. Suggest marking node for hardware replacement when cooled.

maria: good catch. I'll open a ticket to replace GPU unit and label node as `hardware-suspect`. Ticket created: HW-3421.

ajay: monitoring streaming p95/p99 now. initial effect: p95 unchanged ~210ms, p99 dropped from 2.8s -> 650ms after route override. throughput for small model increases CPU cost but acceptable for now.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied (route override + cordon) — latency improving. Metrics: p99=640ms, error_rate=0.6% (was 3.4%).

lisa: assign follow-ups: 
- hardware ticket HW-3421 (maria)
- improve streaming fallback to CPU path (jordan)
- add node-level ECC alert threshold to trigger preemptive drain (ajay)

maria: noted. also will coordinate with facilities to check rack cooling.

oliver: customer messages sent: org-amber acknowledged, wants postmortem if degradation >30m.

ajay: handing off to night oncall @lisa in 10m. briefed: node cordoned, route override expires at +10m, watch p99 and re-enable normal routing if stable <500ms for 5m.

lisa: taking handoff. thanks. I'll keep the channel updated. setting a paging rule: escalate if p99 > 1s for 3 consecutive mins.

opsbot: schedule note created: follow-up review meeting tomorrow 10:00 UTC (incident review, HW plan).

jordan: one more: capturing kernel logs and nvml dump for postmortem. saving to s3://redwood-incident-logs/2045678901/ .

maria: facilities confirmed increased CRAC setpoint in that rack earlier today for maintenance. opening facilities ticket FAC-889. could be related.

lisa: current status: degraded -> improving. keeping cordon until node replaced. will update last_message_ts when we close. :thumbsup:

ajay: thanks team. moving to monitoring.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (2045679250): route override removed at +20m, node remains cordoned and scheduled for replacement. Final metrics: peak p99=2.8s, duration above SLO=12m, estimated impacted requests ~9.4k, impacted customers flagged: org-amber (major), org-verdant (minor). Postmortem assigned.
